templates.name: Skeletal Retainers
templates.summary: Four retainers defend the servants’ hall under a brittle command seal.

cues.signal: Four place settings gather dust except for fresh bone scratches beneath the table.
cues.inference: Skeletal guards rise if the command seal is crossed.

stakes.headline: Break, turn, or avoid the retainers before they ring the keep bell.

approaches.label: Fight the skeletal retainers

onSuccess.summary: The retainers fall and the servants’ hall clears.

onPartial.summary: The guards fall, but the bell rings once and the party becomes rattled.

onFailure.summary: Damage is applied and Keep Alert rises.

approaches.lockout: Every round changes HP or Keep Alert; defeated mobs cannot respawn at the cleared node.

approaches.label: Turn the command seal with Religion

onSuccess.summary: The seal recognizes a higher command and the retainers stand down.

onFailure.summary: The seal cracks, locking this method and raising alert.

approaches.lockout: The cracked seal cannot be invoked again.

approaches.label: Close the iron service door and reroute

onSuccess.summary: The party bars the door and accepts a detour.

onFailure.summary: The route is unavailable; the UI removes this option and explains why.

approaches.lockout: Withdrawal commits once or becomes unavailable because the named route closes.

config.procedure: roll d20; apply advantage/disadvantage; add ability and proficiency when relevant; meet or exceed DC/AC
config.combatObjective: reduce all active retainer HP to zero or invert the command seal

forcedTerminal.summary: The party slams the service door after the bell rings; the encounter ends with a detour.

resolution.antiRepeatRule: A failed check changes the mechanism, route, danger, resource, or opportunity before another roll.

example.telegraphProse: Fresh scratches beneath dusty place settings and a taut bell cord reveal the retainers before they rise.
example.stakesProse: Fight, invoke the command seal at DC 14, or bar the service door and accept the west-stair detour.
example.resolutionProse: HP and Keep Alert update each round; turn six forces the door-barred exit rather than indefinite initiative.
example.receiptProse: The ledger marks the hall cleared or rerouted and records milestone progress plus loot, condition, or quest state.

templates.name: Pendulum Chapel Trap
templates.summary: A visible pressure seam releases consecrated pendulum blades across the nave.

cues.signal: Dust stops at a clean line while copper hooks and a ceiling slit frame the nave.
cues.inference: A pressure-triggered blade sweep crosses the route.

stakes.headline: Disarm, bypass, or abandon the chapel route before the pendulum releases.

approaches.label: Disable the gear train with thieves’ tools

check.modifierSource: character.dexterity + proficiency when Thieves Tools applies

onSuccess.summary: The gear train locks and the nave opens.

onPartial.summary: The blades lock, but the tool tip snaps; success remains committed.

onFailure.summary: The blades sweep, a DC 14 Dexterity save resolves damage, and the panel bends shut.

approaches.lockout: Failure bends the panel shut; this exact tools approach cannot repeat.

approaches.label: Jam the blades with the iron lectern

onSuccess.summary: The lectern jams the sweep and the party passes.

onFailure.summary: The lectern slips and release danger advances.

approaches.lockout: A failed jam changes the lectern state and increases the next DC.

approaches.label: Take the flooded sacristy bypass

onSuccess.summary: The party avoids the trap through a flooded, resource-costly bypass.

onFailure.summary: The route is unavailable; the UI removes this option and explains why.

approaches.lockout: Withdrawal commits once or becomes unavailable because the named route closes.

config.procedure: roll d20; apply advantage/disadvantage; add ability and proficiency when relevant; meet or exceed DC/AC

forcedTerminal.summary: The pendulum releases once, damage resolves, and the route opens behind the spent mechanism.

resolution.antiRepeatRule: A failed check changes the mechanism, route, danger, resource, or opportunity before another roll.

example.telegraphProse: A clean dust line, wall hooks, and the ceiling slit show exactly where the pendulum will sweep.
example.stakesProse: Disable at DC 15, jam at DC 13 with the lectern, or spend a torch on the flooded sacristy route.
example.resolutionProse: A failed disable queues the DC 14 save and closes that panel; at four turns the blade fires once and becomes spent.
example.receiptProse: Receipts mark the hazard disarmed, jammed, bypassed, or triggered and record route, tool, injury, milestone, and item changes.

templates.name: Portcullis Oath Check
templates.summary: A speaking portcullis tests whether visitors can prove lawful purpose.

cues.signal: The gate recites three lawful purposes and asks the party to name its witness.
cues.inference: The obstacle accepts social or historical proof, not only force.

stakes.headline: Convince, recall, or abandon the oath gate before it brands the party trespassers.

approaches.label: State a lawful purpose and name a witness

onSuccess.summary: The gate accepts the purpose and opens.

onPartial.summary: The gate opens but summons a spectral escort.

onFailure.summary: The claim is rejected and cannot be repeated unchanged.

approaches.lockout: A rejected witness is recorded; the party must present different proof or choose another route.

approaches.label: Recall the founder’s exception with History

onSuccess.summary: The forgotten exception compels the portcullis to rise.

onFailure.summary: The misquotation advances the brand and changes the clause state.

approaches.lockout: The same quotation cannot be rolled again; a corrected source is required.

approaches.label: Leave for the roof-walk approach

onSuccess.summary: The party abandons the gate and climbs into the storm.

onFailure.summary: The route is unavailable; the UI removes this option and explains why.

approaches.lockout: Withdrawal commits once or becomes unavailable because the named route closes.

config.procedure: roll d20; apply advantage/disadvantage; add ability and proficiency when relevant; meet or exceed DC/AC

forcedTerminal.summary: The gate brands the party and locks; the encounter ends with a removal quest.

resolution.antiRepeatRule: A failed check changes the mechanism, route, danger, resource, or opportunity before another roll.

example.telegraphProse: The speaking gate lists accepted purposes and asks for a witness, making the social obstacle and proof structure explicit.
example.stakesProse: Persuade at DC 14, invoke a known historical exception at DC 12, or take the dangerous roof walk.
example.resolutionProse: Rejected evidence is logged and cannot be recycled; four turns fill the brand clock and close the gate conclusively.
example.receiptProse: The system records opened access, escort, brand, or detour along with milestone and quest progression.

templates.name: Rising Black Cistern
templates.summary: Cursed water rises while the party searches for a drain wheel.

cues.signal: BLACK WATER 2/6; at full, the lower vault floods.
cues.inference: The hazard is a visible deadline.

cues.signal: A rusted chain leads from the drain grille to a wheel above the waterline.
cues.inference: The environment exposes a mechanical solution.

stakes.headline: Open the drain, reach the balcony, or retreat before the cistern fills.

approaches.label: Turn the rusted drain wheel

onSuccess.summary: The drain opens and the lower vault remains accessible.

onPartial.summary: The drain opens, but the effort causes exhaustion.

onFailure.summary: The water rises and the wheel bends, increasing the next DC.

approaches.lockout: Wheel state changes after failure; the same DC is never rolled from the same state.

approaches.label: Climb to the reliquary balcony

onSuccess.summary: The party escapes upward but loses the lower route.

onFailure.summary: The climber slips and the water rises.

approaches.lockout: A failed climb consumes or relocates the rope and alters advantage.

approaches.label: Retreat through the intake tunnel

onSuccess.summary: The party leaves safely but forfeits lower-vault access.

onFailure.summary: The route is unavailable; the UI removes this option and explains why.

approaches.lockout: Withdrawal commits once or becomes unavailable because the named route closes.

config.procedure: roll d20; apply advantage/disadvantage; add ability and proficiency when relevant; meet or exceed DC/AC

forcedTerminal.summary: The water fills the chamber and carries the party to the balcony; the lower vault is lost.

resolution.antiRepeatRule: A failed check changes the mechanism, route, danger, resource, or opportunity before another roll.

example.telegraphProse: The visible water clock and chain-to-wheel geometry show both deadline and solution.
example.stakesProse: Open the wheel at DC 15, climb at DC 13 and lose the lower route, or retreat and forfeit its loot.
example.resolutionProse: Every failure raises the water; at six turns the flood carries the party out and permanently resolves the location state.
example.receiptProse: Receipts reconcile water, routes, exhaustion, lower-vault access, milestones, and reliquary rewards.

templates.name: Duel with the Castellan’s Heir
templates.summary: A spectral heir demands satisfaction but can be released by proving the true murderer.

cues.signal: The heir names the formal duel law and points to the blood-stained witness gallery.
cues.inference: Combat, surrender, and evidentiary release are valid terminals.

stakes.headline: Defeat, release, or yield to the heir before the gallery seals.

approaches.label: Fight under the heir’s duel law

onSuccess.summary: The heir yields and opens the gallery.

onPartial.summary: The heir yields, but the champion is wounded.

onFailure.summary: The champion takes damage and the gallery seal advances.

approaches.lockout: Combat rounds always change HP or the gallery clock.

approaches.label: Present the kitchen ledger as murder proof

onSuccess.summary: The heir accepts the proof, releases the duel, and entrusts the signet.

onFailure.summary: The proof is rejected and cannot be presented again unchanged.

approaches.lockout: Rejected evidence requires new corroboration; the same ledger topic cannot loop.

approaches.label: Yield and surrender the stolen signet

onSuccess.summary: The duel ends and the heir takes the signet.

onFailure.summary: The route is unavailable; the UI removes this option and explains why.

approaches.lockout: Withdrawal commits once or becomes unavailable because the named route closes.

config.procedure: roll d20; apply advantage/disadvantage; add ability and proficiency when relevant; meet or exceed DC/AC
config.combatObjective: force formal surrender or prove the murderer

forcedTerminal.summary: The gallery seals; the heir withdraws and the duel ends with a new route objective.

resolution.antiRepeatRule: A failed check changes the mechanism, route, danger, resource, or opportunity before another roll.

example.telegraphProse: The heir announces the law, the surrender price, and the evidence gallery before drawing steel.
example.stakesProse: Fight, present the kitchen ledger at DC 14 with corroboration, or yield the stolen signet to end the duel.
example.resolutionProse: Combat changes HP; rejected evidence locks; and the eighth turn seals the gallery and closes the encounter.
example.receiptProse: The outcome records the heir’s durable state, signet ownership, gallery access, milestone progress, and follow-up quest.

templates.name: The Four Saints Door
templates.summary: Four movable saint reliefs encode the keep’s order of succession.

cues.signal: A nursery rubbing names the saints by season, while each relief holds a different harvest tool.
cues.inference: The puzzle has discoverable ordering evidence.

stakes.headline: Open the saint door, spend a bypass resource, or retreat before the curse brands a false succession.

approaches.label: Order the saints using the nursery rubbing

onSuccess.summary: The correct succession opens the library.

onPartial.summary: The door opens while a minor curse attaches to the solver.

onFailure.summary: The wrong order is recorded, excluded, and advances the curse.

approaches.lockout: Identical arrangements are rejected without a roll; failed patterns cannot repeat.

approaches.label: Spend the wax Saint Key

onSuccess.summary: The consumed key bypasses the sequence and opens the door.

onFailure.summary: An invalid key is not consumed but becomes unavailable for this door.

approaches.lockout: The unique key can be used once; invalid provenance disables the option.

approaches.label: Leave the ancestral wing

onSuccess.summary: The party leaves and opens a clue-finding objective.

onFailure.summary: The route is unavailable; the UI removes this option and explains why.

approaches.lockout: Withdrawal commits once or becomes unavailable because the named route closes.

config.procedure: roll d20; apply advantage/disadvantage; add ability and proficiency when relevant; meet or exceed DC/AC

forcedTerminal.summary: The curse marks a false heir and the door locks; a cleansing quest begins.

resolution.antiRepeatRule: A failed check changes the mechanism, route, danger, resource, or opportunity before another roll.

example.telegraphProse: The nursery rubbing and harvest tools provide a fair evidence chain for the succession order.
example.stakesProse: Solve at DC 13 with inspected symbols, consume the unique wax key, or leave and search for more evidence.
example.resolutionProse: Wrong arrangements are stored and blocked; after four attempts the false-heir mark commits and the door locks.
example.receiptProse: The receipt preserves solution or bypass method, key state, library access, curse state, milestone, and follow-up.

templates.name: The Hollow Castellan
templates.summary: The keep’s ruler alternates martial and oath-bound phases around a visible heart reliquary.

cues.signal: From the witness gallery, the party sees the heart reliquary, two oath braziers, and the postern stair.
cues.inference: The boss objectives and flee route are visible before commitment.

cues.signal: The heir warns that the Castellan must answer a true accusation after both braziers go dark.
cues.inference: A proof-based parley terminal is available after setup.

cues.signal: BOSS RULE: martial and oath phases alternate; repeated tactics lose advantage.
cues.inference: Phase structure and anti-repeat rule are explicit.

stakes.headline: End the curse, expose the Castellan, or escape before the keep seals its heart.

approaches.label: Extinguish both oath braziers and break the reliquary

onSuccess.summary: The reliquary breaks and the keep’s curse ends.

onPartial.summary: The curse ends, but the heir spends their spirit to hold the heart open.

onFailure.summary: Resolved damage lands and the heart seal advances.

approaches.lockout: Each phase changes HP, brazier state, or heart-seal progress; repeated tactics lose advantage.

approaches.label: Accuse the Castellan with the murder proof

onSuccess.summary: The true accusation compels confession and dissolves the oath-body.

onFailure.summary: The accusation fails, consumes the public proof, and accelerates the seal.

approaches.lockout: The proof is spent whether accepted or rejected; no accusation loop is possible.

approaches.label: Escape down the postern stair

onSuccess.summary: The party escapes while the keep remains cursed.

onFailure.summary: The route is unavailable; the UI removes this option and explains why.

approaches.lockout: Withdrawal commits once or becomes unavailable because the named route closes.

config.procedure: roll d20; apply advantage/disadvantage; add ability and proficiency when relevant; meet or exceed DC/AC
config.combatObjective: extinguish braziers then reduce reliquary HP to zero or compel confession

forcedTerminal.summary: The heart seals and expels the party as oath-bound servants; the fight ends with a liberation quest.

resolution.antiRepeatRule: A failed check changes the mechanism, route, danger, resource, or opportunity before another roll.

example.telegraphProse: The gallery vista shows braziers, reliquary, and postern while the heir explains the accusation condition and status panel reveals phase rules.
example.stakesProse: Break the curse in combat, spend validated murder proof after setup, or escape and leave the keep cursed.
example.resolutionProse: The heart-seal clock bounds twelve turns; all attacks, proof, and routes mutate state, and the bound creates a liberation quest.
example.receiptProse: Victory or confession emits boss loot, milestone, dungeon, curse, NPC, and quest receipts; retreat and defeat remain durable.

templates.name: Lantern Pilgrim at the Cross-Stair
templates.summary: A neutral ghost offers guidance but may be a mimic wearing a pilgrim’s memory.

cues.signal: The pilgrim’s lantern casts two shadows, one pointing toward a safe stair and one toward a sealed pantry.
cues.inference: The apparition may be divided or false.

stakes.headline: Trust, test, or avoid the pilgrim before the lantern chooses a stair.

approaches.label: Test the pilgrim with Insight

onSuccess.summary: The party identifies the ghost’s truth and learns the safe stair.

onPartial.summary: The safe stair is revealed, but the lantern cry raises Keep Alert.

onFailure.summary: The reading fails and changes the clue state; Insight cannot repeat unchanged.

approaches.lockout: Once the apparition reacts, the social state changes and the same Insight check is invalid.

approaches.label: Offer the recovered pilgrim name

onSuccess.summary: The named spirit becomes a temporary guide.

onFailure.summary: The name is wrong; the spirit departs and this route closes.

approaches.lockout: The name can be offered once and is then confirmed or spent.

approaches.label: Avoid both marked stairs

onSuccess.summary: The party backtracks safely while alert rises.

onFailure.summary: The route is unavailable; the UI removes this option and explains why.

approaches.lockout: Withdrawal commits once or becomes unavailable because the named route closes.

config.procedure: roll d20; apply advantage/disadvantage; add ability and proficiency when relevant; meet or exceed DC/AC

forcedTerminal.summary: The lantern chooses and vanishes; the party is placed on one persistent route and the encounter closes.

resolution.antiRepeatRule: A failed check changes the mechanism, route, danger, resource, or opportunity before another roll.

example.telegraphProse: The double shadow turns a random ghost meeting into a readable trust problem.
example.stakesProse: Test at DC 12, offer the one-use name at DC 10, or backtrack while accepting alert.
example.resolutionProse: The apparition changes after every attempt; the fourth turn selects a persistent route and removes the event.
example.receiptProse: The result records route, pilgrim identity, ghost-light, alert, milestone, and any pantry escape hook.
